![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14097078/assets/6f1cd478f596aa904dc9b1e254c2eb2873b264935cc11b2c3480fc3560d08d55.png)

The graph of $y=f(x),$ shown above, consists of three line segments. Find the value of ${\int }_{-4}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x.$
questions.worked_solution:
We divide the interval of integration into $4$ regions: the line segment for $x\in [-4,-3),$ the line segment for $x\in [-3,-2],$ the line segment for $x\in [-2,1],$ and the line segment for $x\in (1,4].$ Therefore, we can write the required integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{-4}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-4}^{-3}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{-3}^{-2}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}+{{{\int }_{-2}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{3}}+{{{\int }_{1}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{4}}
$$

- The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-4,-3).$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}(bh) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(1\cdot 3) \\  & =1.5.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have

$$
{\int }_{-4}^{-3}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{1}=-1.5.
$$

- The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-3,-2].$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}(bh) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(1\cdot 3) \\  & =1.5.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $3$rd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-2,1].$ The corresponding region is a trapezoid, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{3} & =\frac{1}{2}(a+b)h \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(4+1)(3) \\  & =7.5.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $4$th integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in (1,4].$ The corresponding region is a rectangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{4} & =bh \\  & =3\cdot 2 \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have

$$
{\int }_{1}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{4}=-6.
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-4}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =-{A}_{1}+{A}_{2}+{A}_{3}-{A}_{4} \\  & =-1.5+1.5+7.5-6 \\  & =1.5.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

questions.worked_solution:
The graph consists of $2$ parts: the line segment for $x\in [-3,1)$ and the arc of the semi-circle for $x\in (1,5].$ So, we can use the additive property of integrals to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-3}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-3}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={{{\int }_{-3}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{1}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-3,1).$ The corresponding region is a triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}(bh) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(4\cdot 3) \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in (1,5].$ The corresponding region is a semi-circle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\pi \cdot (2)^{2} \\  & =2\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-3}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}+{A}_{2} \\  & =6+2\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

- The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =bh-\frac{1}{4}\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =(2)(2)-\frac{1}{4}\pi (2)^{2} \\  & =4-\pi .\end{aligned}

$$

$$

We divide the interval of integration into $3$ regions: the arc of the semi-circle for $x\in [-3,1),$ the line segment for $x\in [1,3],$ and the line segment for $x\in [3,6].$ Therefore, we can use the additive property of integrals to write

$$
{\int }_{-3}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-3}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{1}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}+{{{\int }_{3}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{3}}.
$$

- The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-3,1).$   The corresponding region is a combination of a semi-circle of radius $2$ and a rectangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}\pi {r}^{2}+bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\pi (2)^{2}+4(1) \\  & =2\pi +4.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [1,3].$   The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula 

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}(bh) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(2\cdot 2) \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $3$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [3,6].$   The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula 

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{3} & =\frac{1}{2}(bh) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(3\cdot 3) \\  & =\frac{9}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have

$$
{\int }_{3}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{3}=-\frac{9}{2}.
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-3}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}+{A}_{2}-{A}_{3} \\  & =2\pi +4+2-\frac{9}{2} \\  & =\frac{4\pi +3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14097078/assets/ad45cbdcd126df931f1a35c60ca12b45d520a2a0a5cddf4fa012c0515d3024c7.png)

The graph of $y=f(x),$ shown above, consists of two line segments. Find the value of $\displaystyle \int_{0}^{4} f(x)\: \textrm{d}x.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The graph consists of two parts: the line segment for $x \in [0,2)$ and the line segment for $x \in [2,4].$ Therefore, we can write the required integral as follows:

$$
\int_{0}^{4} f(x)\: \textrm{d}x = \underbrace{\int_{0}^{2} f(x)\: \textrm{d}x}_{A_1} + \underbrace{\int_{2}^{4} f(x)\: \textrm{d}x}_{-A_2}.
$$

- The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x \in [0,2).$ The corresponding region is a rectangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =bh \\  & =2\cdot 2 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x \in [2,4].$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\cdot 2 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have 

$$
\int_{2}^{4} f(x)\: \textrm{d}x =-A_2 = -2.
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}-{A}_{2} \\  & =4-2 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14097078/assets/36c6a1c84e0b0c32a5fd35fd422645f60340da6d205dd8cc31054cd558c2f5f9.png)

Given the graph of $y=f(x)$ above, find the value of $\displaystyle \int_{-4}^4 f(x) \,\textrm{d}x.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The graph consists of four parts: the arc of a semi-circle for $x\in [-4,0],$ a line segment for $x\in (0,2),$ a line segment for $x\in (2,4],$ and the point at $x=2.$ So, we can use the additive property of integrals to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-4}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-4}^{0}f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={{{\int }_{-4}^{0}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{0}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{2}}+0+{{{\int }_{2}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x \in [-4,0].$ The corresponding region is a semi-circle with a radius of $2,$ so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot \pi \cdot {2}^{2} \\  & =2\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

- The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x \in (0,2).$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\cdot 2 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have

$$
\int_{0}^{2} f(x)\: \textrm{d}x = -A_2 = -2.
$$

- The $3$rd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x \in (2,4].$  The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{3} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\cdot 2 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-4}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}-{A}_{2}+{A}_{3} \\  & =2\pi -2+2 \\  & =2\pi .\end{aligned}
$$
